Hold the kind and span claims of the install-page pin (#289)

Make the self-checks of tools/test-install-page.py hold what its
docstrings say about the reader pin of check 7, and word those
docstrings so that they claim no more than the checks hold. The gate,
tools/check-install-page.py, is byte identical, so GATE_SHA256 stays
88f416948b41fcf9464de097d68cfa9f34e6a4e2a3284ce215582d220fe2d5d7, its
sha256, and READER_SHA256 stays as it is. READER_SHA256 maps each of
the 27 names that the reader pin holds to its own digest, so this
message lists none of them.

- Capture tuple, list and dict when the test is imported, as
  PLAIN_CONTAINERS beside PLAIN_TYPES, so that plain_data(), as
  pin_value() does, compares the exact type of a value by identity
  with a type that the test captured when it was imported
  (PLAIN_TYPES, PLAIN_CONTAINERS, PIN_KINDS).
- Add capture_problems(): with re.Pattern, types.ModuleType, the
  test's REPO_ROOT, str, bytes, int, float, bool, tuple, list or dict
  rebound to a stand-in, 1 name at a time, pin_value() must still
  write a real value of that kind as before and refuse an instance of
  the stand-in, and each name must be restored once the last of them
  has been rebound. control_problems() holds the 1st rule for each of
  the 11 names and the restore for each of them but dict, the last,
  which the finally clause restores. The exact type of a value, and
  type(None), are read with the builtin type(), which a rebinding of a
  builtin can change, a class that the reader pin does not see
  (residual 2); no check holds the capture of type.
- Derive refusal cases from the 3 capture tuples: for each of their 13
  kinds, an object whose class gives the kind as its __class__, and,
  for each of the 10 kinds that FINAL_KINDS does not name, an instance
  of a bare subclass, so that each kind test of pin_value() and
  plain_data() must match the exact type. FINAL_KINDS names the kinds
  of these tuples that Python lets no class subclass (bool, NoneType
  and re.Pattern), not every such kind that Python has. A subclass
  that cannot be made fails the check, and so does a kind of
  FINAL_KINDS that Python lets a class subclass or that is in none of
  these tuples. The 19 committed refused values are kept.
- Run the 2 replacements of REQUESTED_FILES on 3 base gates: the
  committed gate, one in which its statement shares its line with
  LOADED_SEGMENTS and REDIRECT_TARGETS and a comment, and one in which
  it spans 3 lines with a comment after it. Each built gate must first
  pass the reader pin and have the layout of its builder's docstring,
  each of the 2 parts of that layout checked apart (on the shared-line
  gate, the line of REQUESTED_FILES, parsed alone, ends with the 3
  statements in that order, and a comment follows them; on the
  reflowed gate, the statement spans exactly 3 lines, and a comment
  follows it), and each gate with the statement replaced must keep the
  comments of its base gate. The builders' only source is GATE_BYTES,
  so neither states or checks a rule of its own about its source.
- Make binding_sites(), which the reader pin reads, walk the whole
  syntax tree and read each string that a node other than an import or
  an alias holds as a name that it binds, but a name that is read, a
  type comment and the fields of UNBOUND_FIELDS, and of an import only
  the name that each alias binds, so it fails closed and finds a type
  parameter. Hold it with SECOND_BINDINGS, 26 sources that each bind
  or declare REQUESTED_FILES 1 more time, a nonlocal statement, a
  dotted import, a from import, an augmented and an annotated
  assignment, an async for, an async with and a type alias among
  them, in each of which it must
  find the name exactly 2 times, and with LINE_BINDINGS, 17 sources,
  each with the lines at which it must find the name: 14 sources with
  a 2nd or 3rd binding on the line of a binding, by each kind of node
  that binds or declares a name on 1 line, a lambda parameter
  included, 1 source with a 2nd binding on the next line, and a from
  import of a module of that name and an import of it as qz, which
  bind another name.
- Hold the binding check of the reader pin itself with GATE_BINDINGS,
  6 sources that each add a 2nd binding of REQUESTED_FILES to the
  committed gate and leave 1 statement at its top level that binds it
  and its value as they were: on the line of its statement, an
  assignment expression, a comprehension and a lambda parameter, and
  after the last line, an assignment inside a false conditional, a for
  over nothing and a parameter of a def. The reader pin must give
  exactly 1 problem for each, which starts by naming the lines at
  which the gate binds the name: the line of its statement and the
  line of the source added.
- Hold the whole problem that the reader pin gives for PIN_PLAIN on
  each base gate: that REQUESTED_FILES differs from its pin, with the
  sha256 of reader_pin_text() of the statement and value of PIN_PLAIN
  and the digest that READER_SHA256 records.
- Add control_problems(): with a name of the test rebound to a
  stand-in for 1 call, each rule of capture_problems(),
  pin_value_problems() and scope_sentence_problems() that its
  docstring lists must make that check fail, each part of the
  shared-line layout and of the reflowed layout included, each
  broken alone by its own stand-ins, and both parts of the shared-line
  layout broken together, so an edit that removes such a rule from its
  check alone fails. binding_sites() stand-ins that find each binding
  2 times, the 1st binding of each name 1 more time or each binding 1
  line lower tell the exact rules of SECOND_BINDINGS and LINE_BINDINGS
  from another count, from a bound and from a count of lines. Reader
  pin stand-ins that find no problem, give each problem 2 times or
  name another line and another digest hold the rules of exactly 1
  problem of GATE_BINDINGS and of the replacements, with its lines and
  its digest.
  The rules of the span and of the restore are held by those checks as
  they run. An edit of a check and of its control together rests on
  review (residual 4).
- Rewrite the fixture PIN_SUBCLASS as 1 simple statement with the same
  meaning, a deliberate change of its contract: a class statement
  cannot follow a semicolon, so the committed form does not parse on
  the shared-line gate.
- Add to pin_value()'s docstring that it writes a module, a class or a
  path by its name, so a helper that such a module, class or path
  carries is in no digest here, and mark its refused values as
  examples. The pin holds the values that a reviewed gate defines in
  ordinary code, and scope_sentence_problems() fails each docstring of
  the file that says so without the words "a module, a class or a path
  by its name".
- Rewrite the module docstring's account of the kind tests and of
  pin_value_problems() with only what these checks hold.
- Leave .github/squash/269.txt unchanged: this change edits no merged
  squash record.

Checks, each with its expected outcome:

- python3 -I tools/test-install-page.py: exit 0, "all 623 cases".
- python3 -I tools/check-install-page.py: exit 0, and its sha256
  equals GATE_SHA256 before and after this change.
- Each mutant that the description names, 1 or 2 exact replacements
  in a copy of the test: in each tree, the outcome that the
  description gives for it, by the command that the description gives
  for that outcome.
- python3 -I tools/check-pr-text.py on the description and on this
  message: exit 0, 0 defects.
